proposedContracts.name: matches native framecrc, WAV, AIFF, AU, W64 and raw output with output -ss/-t for mono and stereo HEDR/HDR8 files, NOTE, unknown and SD_2 chunks
proposedContracts.scope: nsp decode to framecrc/s16le/w64/wav/aiff/au with output -ss/-t; HEDR/HDR8, SDA_/SD_A/SD_2/SDAB, unknown-chunk and NOTE quirks; metadata refusal for wav/aiff/au

proposedContracts.name: refuses -c copy (native copy timestamps use 1/90000) and input -ss before any output, and matches native refusal statuses
proposedContracts.scope: copy, input seek and zero-sample refusals; native EINVAL (host) / 234 and INVALIDDATA 183 statuses; partial-frame refusal

proposedContracts.name: leaves FORM DS16 heads undetected where another native probe ties nsp_probe at 100, and matches native -f nsp on them
proposedContracts.scope: FORM DS16 heads with 16 byte-8 form types that aiff, iff, wsvqa, rl2 or wc3 also score 100: native 183 asserted, refused undeclared with no output, -f nsp framecrc byte-exact; 3 near misses detected and byte-exact in both. Wave 2 branch wave2/fmt-nsp.

notes: Probe precedence 24: the FORM head overlaps aiff (30) and iff (26); confirm reads 8 bytes and is false for AIFF/AIFC, MAUD, short inputs and a bare 4-byte FORM (superseded by the audit note: it now reads up to 12 bytes).
Native EINVAL statuses are asserted as 256 - os.constants.errno.EINVAL on the host; EdgeFFmpeg uses the Linux value 234.

Setup: Node 22.23.5 was the sandbox default and bootstrap requires 24+; used preinstalled /opt/node24 (v24.22.3). Bootstrap (npm, submodule, reference) took 4m23s; baseline typecheck/lint/boundaries/registry tests about 1m30s, all passing.
Differential file runs in about 5 s with --maxWorkers=1.

Audit (audit-fmt-b): a FORM DS16 head whose bytes 8..11 hold AIFF, AIFC, an iff form type (8SVX, 16SV, MAUD, PBM , ACBM, DEEP, ILBM, RGB8, ANIM, RGBN), WVQA, RLV2, RLV3 or MOVE also scores 100 in aiff_probe, iff_probe, wsvqa_probe, rl2_probe or wc3_probe; native's tie detects nothing (183) while EdgeFFmpeg detected nsp. The confirm now reads up to 12 bytes and leaves those heads undetected. The audit test ran on macOS arm64 against the pinned darwin reference (sha256 1b86106f…ab92), not on the sandbox linux-x64 build.
